Seat: domain:spec#1

**Declared file surface**: to be established by the taker and ⛔ **declared before the first edit** — the card is about a `-t` named-test invocation, so the landing point may be a gate script, a guard, or documentation, and guessing it here would be this seat choosing the remedy.

⚠️ **SERIAL CONSTRAINT — read this before touching `scripts/`.** The one other `pm:dispatched` card of this lane, objectui#9717 (PR objectui#9724), is **in `scripts/` right now**: `check-doc-component-types.mjs`, `check-registry-bare-name-collisions.mjs`, and suites under `scripts/__tests__/`. ⇒ if your landing point is any of those three, **STOP and report** rather than editing across it. Re-take that list against the live PR before you write — it is a reading of 2026-09-17T20:57Z, ⛔ not a standing fact.

⭐ **Why this card is worth doing carefully rather than quickly.** Its subject is a **FALSE GREEN**: `vitest -t 'name'` exits **0 reporting everything skipped** when the name carries regex metacharacters — and this repo's describe names end in `(objectui#NNNN)`, so the parentheses and `#` make the natural copy-paste silently match nothing. ⇒ a seat that runs a named test to check its own work gets **exit 0 and no test executed**, which is the exact shape this board treats as a broken instrument: ⛔ a zero that is not a reading.

The card notes the sibling cwd trap **IS** guarded, so the asymmetry is the finding: one trap has a gate, its twin does not.

**Fix order, per this repo's standing preference**: first delete the construction that permits the error, then make the correct form the only spelling, and only last add a check. ⭐ A guard that merely warns still leaves the false green spellable.

⛔ Stop conditions: ⛔ never weaken or skip a test to demonstrate the trap; if the repair would change how any existing gate counts or reports, say so and stop — this lane sent a PR back today for exactly that class, and a gate's counting is not a free surface.

## What the card actually bought

⭐ Its subject was a **false green**, and the repair's worth is one comparison: before, the dark leg and the lit control **both exited 0** — `Tests 22 skipped (22)` against `Tests 7 passed | 15 skipped (22)`. ⇒ **the exit code was identical and the reading was not**, so a seat running a named test to check its own work learned nothing. After, the dark leg exits **1** with a refusal box that prints the escaped spelling that works.

The repair lands on **rung 3** of this repo's fix order and says why 1 and 2 were unreachable: rung 1 would have to delete `vitest -t` (upstream, and used by this repo's own timezone pin) or the `(objectui#NNNN)` describe convention (live — ⭐ and deleting it is an **incomplete** fix anyway, since `[`, `|` and `+` trap identically); rung 2 has no repo-owned wrapper every named run passes through, so a wrapper would be a **second** spelling rather than the only one. ⭐ And the check **REFUSES** rather than warns, which is what makes the false green unspellable.

## Declared limits, both of them correct

- ⚠️ An accepted **false positive**: a deliberately grouped regex such as `(a|b) renders` also cannot match its own literal and is refused. Declared in the PR body **and in the verdict message**. Nothing in the tree writes one today.
- ⛔ A **reporter-level** check would close the remaining gap (a filter matching zero tests at *runtime*, not merely one that provably cannot match its own literal at config load) and was **deliberately not taken**, because it changes how every run in this repo reports. ⭐ That is this lane's stop condition applied unprompted — a gate's reporting is not a free surface.

## Carried forward

The `AGENTS.md` prose is preserved **verbatim** as card **objectui#9731** for the `domain:skills` lane, with its placement note and the instruction to land it **unexpanded** — its closing clause points at the instrument instead of restating what the instrument answers, and expanding it would mint a second copy that rots the moment the guard changes, in the one file four published release notes cite as authority.

Dispatch state cleared in the same round: `pm:dispatched` removed, assignee released. The card is closed `completed` by the merge.
